samples.summary: `READ_GATED_METHODS` makes `AttachDocument` authorize as a read, so a viewer-role share link can write to the document via the attach change pack — the one write the webhook exists to refuse
samples.evidence:
`READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument'])` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108) feeds `checkAttribute`'s `needWrite = REVISION_READ_METHODS.has(method) ? true : attr.verb === 'rw' && !READ_GATED_METHODS.has(method)` (line 332-334). Before this change an `AttachDocument` carrying verb `rw` required `link.role === 'editor'` (hasAccess, line 370); now attach is authorized with `needWrite=false`, i.e. any identity with *read* access.

Attack: a holder of a viewer-role share token (or a public-template `previewToken`, which is `listing.shareLink.token` — template.service.ts:1314) does (1) `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` with the token to get a signed `yorkie-share` Yorkie token, (2) builds a bare `@yorkie-js/sdk` client with the project public key that ships in every visitor's bundle, (3) `new Document(key)`, `doc.update(...)` locally, then `client.attach(doc)`. The SDK sends the accumulated local change pack inside the `AttachDocument` RPC (which is precisely why the diff observes attach always carries `rw`), so the webhook is asked with `AttachDocument`/`rw`, answers ALLOW on read access, and the pack is applied server-side. `DetachDocument` is unconditionally allowed (`ALWAYS_ALLOWED_METHOD`, line 66/221 — no token needed at all), so the write loop is detach → mutate → re-attach, unbounded.

Impact: server-side enforcement of "viewer means read-only" does not exist for any non-browser client, on an enforcing deployment. It also undercuts the premise of `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` (template-review.ts:104): every anonymous visitor to a public template card holds a preview token, and an edit puts the listing back into the human-only review queue, so the gallery-drain abuse that gate was written to prevent is still reachable, only at the cost of running a script instead of one HTTP request. The change acknowledges this residual in its own comments (lines 99-106, template-review.ts:85-96) but ships the weakened gate; reporting it because the gate now reads as covered while the viewer-write path stays open.

samples.summary: An unscoped `yorkie-service` token is a blanket allow on every document and every method; the ops scripts mint one and transmit it to the Yorkie server on every RPC
samples.evidence:
`decideService()` returns `ALLOW` immediately when the payload has no `key` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:289-291) — no document check, no verb check, no method check. That covers `PushPull`, `RestoreRevision`/`CreateRevision` (full history rollback), `GetRevision` (snapshots of deleted content) on *any* document key, including keys `parseYorkieDocKey` would reject.

`yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv()` (yorkie-service-token.ts:104) mints exactly such an unscoped token from `process.env.JWT_SECRET` and it is installed on the long-lived clients in `scripts/migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:221`, `scripts/migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:347`, and (via `sideTokenInjector`, copy-yorkie-documents.ts:53) on both clients of `copy-yorkie-documents.ts:255,260`. The credential does not stay in the process: the SDK sends it to whatever `YORKIE_RPC_ADDR`/`--source-rpc-addr`/`--target-rpc-addr` names, on every RPC, over whatever transport that URL specifies (the default in the migration scripts is plaintext `http://localhost:8080`, migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:213). Anyone able to observe that traffic, read the Yorkie server's request logs, or operate a managed/third-party Yorkie obtains deployment-wide read/write on every document for the token's lifetime — and there is no revocation, only expiry. Before this change these scripts sent no token, so this is newly introduced blast radius. There is also no `jti`/`aud` and no per-run allow-list, so nothing bounds replay within the window.

samples.summary: Service tokens carry no `aud`/`iss`, so one deployment's service token is accepted by any deployment sharing `JWT_SECRET` — the exact multi-deployment scenario `copy-yorkie-documents.ts` is built for
samples.evidence: `signYorkieServiceToken` signs only `{ typ, key? }` (yorkie-service-token.ts:66-69) and `verifyYorkieToken` checks only the signature and `typ` (auth.service.ts:96-105) — no audience, issuer, or deployment identifier. `copy-yorkie-documents.ts` exists precisely because "the source and target are different deployments with different secrets" (its own comment), but nothing enforces that: if an operator sets `SOURCE_JWT_SECRET` and `TARGET_JWT_SECRET` to the same value (staging restored from a prod dump, or a same-deployment copy), the unscoped credential minted for one side authorizes every document on the other. Binding `aud` to the deployment's own origin (`WAFFLEBASE_API_ORIGIN` already exists) and verifying it would make cross-deployment presentation fail closed.

samples.summary: `decideService` ignores the verb, so a document-scoped service token grants write even on read-only server paths
samples.evidence: The scoped branch compares only `attr.key !== identity.key` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:306-314) and never looks at `attr.verb`. `YorkieService.withDocument` accepts `syncMode: 'readonly'` (yorkie.service.ts:10,101) and several callers use it purely to read a document, yet the token it hands the SDK (yorkie.service.ts:83-87) is write-capable for that key. Threading the intended verb into the payload (e.g. `verb: 'r'` for `syncMode: 'readonly'`) would make an intercepted read-path token unable to mutate the document at all, which is the stated goal of the `key` scoping.

samples.summary: The service credential's lifetime is governed by the operator-facing `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` knob, so tuning end-user token UX silently extends a deployment-wide credential
samples.evidence: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` takes `expiresIn` from `process.env.YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN ?? '10m'` (yorkie-service-token.ts:106) and `YorkieService` reads the same key (yorkie.service.ts:60-62). That variable is documented purely as "lifetime of the short-lived Yorkie auth-webhook token minted by GET /auth/yorkie-token" (packages/backend/README.md:98-100, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:184), so an operator who raises it to reduce token-refresh churn for browsers also lengthens the validity window of the unscoped, non-revocable, all-documents ops credential from finding 2 with no indication that they did. A separate constant/variable for the service token would decouple the two.

samples.summary: New comments assert the auth webhook "ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default", the opposite of the default this same change establishes — a misleading security-posture claim in new code
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:447 (added by this change) says "the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either", and packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:63-64 (new file) says "the webhook allows everything until a deployment both registers its methods and sets `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`". `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:30) returns true for unset, so enforce is now the default and `=true` is not required. The pre-existing packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40-42 goes further and still claims "with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary", which the notes counterpart explicitly retracts as wrong. Leaving both readings in the tree is how a later contributor concludes either that the client-side proxy is the real gate, or that an unconfigured deployment is not enforcing — both wrong in the unsafe direction.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is present as described. `READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument'])` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108) feeds `needWrite = REVISION_READ_METHODS.has(method) ? true : attr.verb === 'rw' && !READ_GATED_METHODS.has(method)` (lines 332-334), so an `AttachDocument` with verb `rw` is evaluated with `needWrite=false`, and `hasAccess` line 370 (`return needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`) then short-circuits the only viewer/editor role check in the enforced path. The vector is reachable: `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:82-90) is unauthenticated and mints a Yorkie token from any share token regardless of role, and `previewToken` is literally `listing.shareLink?.token` (template.service.ts:1314) handed to every visitor of a public template. Nothing guards the change pack carried inside the attach RPC — `PushPull` only refuses writes after attach (spec.ts:314) — and `DetachDocument` is unconditionally allowed before token verification (lines 66, 221), so the detach → mutate → re-attach write loop is unbounded. The repo's own docs confirm rather than refute the residual (yorkie-auth-webhook.md:310-317; template-review.ts:88-100). No refutation ground applies: code is present, no guard makes it unreachable, and a weakened write/role gate on a share link is squarely in the security lens's authorization lane at critical impact.

verdict.reason: Every claim checks out against the repository. `decideService()` at packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:289-291 returns ALLOW immediately when the service-token payload has no `key`, short-circuiting the method check (294), the fail-closed empty-attribute branch (299-305), and the per-key scope comparison (306-314) — so an unscoped `yorkie-service` token authorizes PushPull, GetRevision/ListRevisions, and any other method on any document key, including keys parseYorkieDocKey would reject. `signYorkieServiceToken` (yorkie-service-token.ts:61-70) omits `key` when none is passed, and `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` (104-116) never passes one, so it mints exactly that unscoped credential from process.env.JWT_SECRET. It is installed on long-lived clients at scripts/migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:221 (rpcAddr defaulting to plaintext http://localhost:8080 at line 213, overridable via YORKIE_RPC_ADDR), and copy-yorkie-documents.ts:40-54 does the same for both source and target clients. The SDK transmits the token on every RPC, so an observer of that traffic, the Yorkie server's logs, or a third-party/managed Yorkie operator gains deployment-wide read/write for the token lifetime; the payload type (yorkie-service-token.ts:33-55) carries no jti/aud and there is no allow-list or revocation. No guard elsewhere blocks this path: decide() at 241-243 routes service tokens into decideService ahead of all other checks. The code's own comments (yorkie-service-token.ts:24-28, yorkie-auth.controller.ts:236-240) state that per-document scoping exists precisely to bound an intercepted token — the unscoped branch removes that bound. This is an authorization/credential-exposure issue, squarely in the security lane, and is not refutable as not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.

searchedFor: Grep 'readOnlyStore|ReadOnlyStore|store/readonly' repo-wide (no access wrapper for sheets; only the datasource result store)
Grep 'canComment' under packages/frontend/src/app/docs (docs gates the equivalent path)
Read packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts and yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts to establish the server-side outcome
finding.summary: Read-only sheet mount still lets a signed-in viewer-role share-link visitor write comment threads/replies/resolutions into the CRDT root; the new YorkieStore.readOnly gate does not cover the comment mutators and no UI gate stands in front of them
finding.evidence: Vector: a visitor who has a Wafflebase account but is NOT a workspace member opens a viewer-role share link to a spreadsheet. shared-document.tsx:283 mounts SheetView readOnly={true}, so the store is new YorkieStore(doc, tabId, true) (sheet-view.tsx:1012). Selection still works in read-only, and the onSelectionChange handler at sheet-view.tsx:1128-1169 auto-opens the comment popover (setCommentPopoverOpen(true), line 1168) whenever the selected cell carries an unresolved thread - it has no readOnly check. The popover is then rendered at sheet-view.tsx:1719 with no readOnly prop, and CommentPopover.tsx:47 computes isReadOnly = currentUser === null, i.e. it only asks 'are you signed in?', never 'what is your share role?'. Because the visitor is signed in, commentAuthor is non-null (sheet-view.tsx:191) and CommentThreadCard renders the reply composer (CommentThreadCard.tsx:188) and the resolve toggle (line 107). Clicking them calls handleCommentReply / handleCommentResolve / handleCommentEdit / handleCommentDelete (sheet-view.tsx:921, 940, 967, 974), which call the RAW store: YorkieStore.addReply -> this.doc.update((root) => applyAddReply(ws, ...)) at yorkie-store.ts:1329, setThreadResolved at :1364, editComment at :1348, deleteComment at :1354. None of these consult the readOnly field this delta introduced, and sheets has no read-only store proxy (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts is the datasource query-result store, not an access wrapper), so the write reaches doc.update and the next PushPull carries verb rw. With YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE unset the webhook refuses it (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:370, needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true), so the observable damage is the viewer's sync wedging - the exact failure this delta exists to remove, just via a different write. With the documented shadow-mode rollout option (YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false) the write PERSISTS, i.e. a viewer-role visitor mutates a document they hold read-only access to. Docs closes

verdict.reason: The client-side facts check out (yorkie-store.ts:1298-1367 comment mutators have no readOnly guard; sheet-view.tsx:1719 renders CommentPopover with no readOnly prop; CommentPopover.tsx:47 only asks "signed in?"), but the authorization gate the finding says is missing exists in the enforced path and denies precisely this write: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:332-338 derives needWrite from the PushPull verb and hasAccess at :370 returns `needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`, so a viewer-role share token's comment write is refused 403; a signed-in non-member on the workspace-token path is refused at :346-359. Enforcement is the default (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-31 — only the literal "false" opts out). The repo's own threat model at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:120-131 states that the client read-only mounts are a correctness boundary, not an access-control one, because a viewer holds the share token plus the bundled public key and can attach with any client — so a UI/store gate cannot be the security control here (the attacker is the viewer, controlling their own client). The only persistence case left is explicit shadow mode (YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false), a documented, boot-warned operator posture (:171-184) in which every write path, cell edits included, is allowed by design without needing this UI path. What remains is real but is a correctness/UX defect (viewer's composer 403s and wedges sync), not an authorization bypass — outside the security lane.

mergedFrom.summary: READ_GATED_METHODS lets a viewer-role share token write: the AttachDocument change pack is applied under a read-only decision

finding.summary: `READ_GATED_METHODS` downgrades `AttachDocument` to a read check, so a share-link `viewer` can write arbitrary content by carrying a change pack in the attach itself
finding.evidence:
Before this change `checkAttribute` computed `needWrite = attr.verb === 'rw' || REVISION_READ_METHODS.has(method)`, so an `AttachDocument` (which Yorkie always sends with verb `rw`) required `link.role === 'editor'`. The new expression at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:332-334 is `REVISION_READ_METHODS.has(method) ? true : attr.verb === 'rw' && !READ_GATED_METHODS.has(method)` — with `READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument'])` (line 108), an attach is now authorized as a read, which `hasAccess` grants any valid viewer link (line 370: `return needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`).

Attack: an anonymous holder of a viewer-role share link POSTs the token to `POST /auth/yorkie-token/share` (auth.controller.ts:82) to mint a `yorkie-share` token, reads the project public key out of any visitor's bundle, then builds a bare `yorkie.Client`, creates a local `Document`, applies arbitrary local changes, and calls `attach`. Yorkie pushes that change pack as part of the AttachDocument RPC; the webhook is consulted with verb `rw` but answers ALLOW because attach is read-gated, so the pack is applied. Detaching and re-attaching repeats it without bound, so the "one pack per attach" bound is not a practical limit — a viewer has effective write access to the document on a fully enforcing deployment.

The change explicitly acknowledges this (`docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md` § Risks, the READ_GATED_METHODS comment, packages/backend/README.md:222), and the public-template-gallery gate `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` now rests on a bound that is narrower than the role it advertises. I could not confirm the residual is closed anywhere else: `PushPull` is the only remaining write gate and it is reached only *after* the attach has already been applied. Flagging because a role check that was previously enforced is now not, and the surface it protects (every viewer-shared document, and every public template document whose `previewToken` is handed to every visitor) is the one the rest

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. READ_GATED_METHODS = new Set(['AttachDocument']) (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108) combined with the gate at yorkie-auth.controller.ts:332-334 makes needWrite false for AttachDocument despite its 'rw' verb, and hasAccess (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:370) returns true for any valid share link when needWrite is false — the link.role === 'editor' check is never reached. The anonymous vector is real: POST /auth/yorkie-token/share is a public endpoint (auth.controller.ts:82; docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:112), so a viewer-link holder can mint a Yorkie token and attach with a hand-rolled client. No guard closes the residual: the repo's own docs state it is open (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:310-320 "The residual is a change pack carried by the attach itself ... the bound is per attach rather than per client"; template-review.ts:87-100 "a client that puts its change pack in the attach itself gets that pack applied, and re-attaching repeats it ... a bound on the residual, not its removal"; packages/backend/README.md:222-226). PushPull is the only remaining write gate and applies only to syncs after the attach. This is authorization/access control — a role check moved out of the enforced path — squarely in the security lane, with critical impact (viewer and preview-token write access to shared and public-template documents). No refutation ground applies: the code is present, unguarded, in-lane, and I found no repository evidence that Yorkie discards an attach-borne change pack.
